children: Germany’s IG Metall union is pushing Volkswagen
to reaffirm its commitment to a labor agreement reached in 2024, adding pressure on management as the carmaker pursues a sweeping restructuring.

Union members voted Friday to activate a provision in the agreement that brings management and labor back to the negotiating table. IG Metall says workers need clarity over whether commitments made under the deal will remain intact as Volkswagen
considers deeper job and production cuts.
The dispute has intensified around plans that could eventually eliminate about 100,000 positions and significantly reduce manufacturing capacity. Volkswagen
is also weighing plant closures as it confronts competition from Chinese automakers, high production costs,costs and increased tariff expenses.

Works council chief Daniela Cavallo rejected the idea that German costs alone were responsible for the company’s difficulties. She called for stronger European measures to protect manufacturers from competitors benefiting from state support in China.
said it welcomed the talks, arguing that discussions would help implement measures agreed in 2024 while addressing new pressures facing the automotive industry.
The earlier agreement followed large-scale walkouts and included about 35,000 job cuts and wage concessions. In exchange, workers secured commitments on investment and the future of some facilities.
IG Metall cannot call strikes under existing labor agreements until the end of the year, media sources reported.

title: IG Metall moves to reopen talks with Volkswagen
